title: Wonders of the East / Astronomical-Calendrical Treatise
shelf_note: A 12th-century illustrated English manuscript (Bodleian; constellation myths after Hyginus plus the Marvels of the East). No tradition or collection is assigned; it fits early-science and astronomy holdings.
structure_note: The images are not a uniform page sequence. Page 20 is a close-up detail: the Gemini miniature plus a sliver of the next column, which shows only the first letters of each line. Page 39 is a full two-page opening in one frame (I3; both pages are read, with printed folio '13' at the top right). Page 58 is a single leaf. The source looks like a set of photographic slides or details rather than a full facsimile, so 77 'pages' do not map one-to-one to leaves.

book_verdict: A beautiful illuminated manuscript, read competently where the image shows a full page (39, 58). Page 20, a cropped detail, carries a translation of two constellation chapters and two illustrations that are not in the image. The image set is a mix of details, openings and single leaves, not a leaf-by-leaf facsimile.

title: Breviarium Romanum
shelf_note: An 1888 Pustet Roman Breviary from Toronto (Kelly Library). It is a mainstream liturgical text, not an esoteric one, but no tradition is assigned and it is a legitimate Latin primary source.
structure_note: 970 pages, 930 with OCR and 900 translated, so roughly 70 pages are missing translation. Page 714 carries a bracketed printed page number [152] from the separately paginated appendix (Officium parvum); this is the volume's own pagination, not a defect.

tr_errors.problem: the first five lines of the page (end of the Marian antiphon) are dropped from the translation

title: Opera [Latin]. Tr: Marsilius Ficinus

title: Sermo generalis de naturis rerum
shelf_note: Thomas of Cantimpré's encyclopedia of nature (a Harvard manuscript): animals, bees, stones and their virtues. It fits medieval natural history and lapidary lore.
structure_note: 200 pages, 193 with OCR and 190 translated. The manuscript's own foliation (25 on page 50, a number on page 98) is consistent with the order. Nothing structural stands out.

book_verdict: The page images are a clear, legible Gothic hand, but the flash-lite OCR misreads its abbreviations throughout. The translation turns the garbles into confident prose: an invented 'seven kings' of the bees, the elders' command reversed, a fox that is 'well' after eating almonds where the text says it dies, and a stone that 'helps the frenzied' where it makes people frantic. An expert would not trust these pages.

title: De quattuor virtutibus cardinalibus, sive De formula honestae vitae
shelf_note: The pseudo-Senecan Formula vitae honestae (Martin of Braga) with a Latin school commentary, printed 1490 (BSB). It fits classical and moral-philosophy holdings, and the 'Seneca' attribution is the period one.
structure_note: 37 pages, 37 with OCR, 34 translated: three pages lack translation. Signature 'b ij' on page 18 is consistent.

book_verdict: The large-type text of Martin of Braga is read well. The dense, abbreviated commentary is read poorly, worst on page 27, where a misread reverses the closing proverb and the commentary's opening is paraphrased rather than transcribed. Usable for the main text; the commentary needs a re-read.
